method_findings.bounded_prune_refill_005-n32: Bounded prune/refill is mostly a local substitution search relative to actual plain-pool-then-prune: 14.654% of sites change text, 13.383% keep the same count with different text, and only 1.2606% add bullets (mean 2.91006 versus 2.89756). All 16 illustrative entries here keep the parent bullet count; two entries repeat other physical cases, so they are neither frequency estimates nor evidence of genuine added-bullet gains. Average paired fraction of variance explained rises by 0.000238264, or 0.02383 percentage points, but useful name/role recoveries coexist with name-precision loss, incoherent arithmetic and unchanged generic failures. Native outcomes versus the actual pruned parent are Hallucination (chat) error 44.7222% versus 44.5124%, Multihop (multi-token) 38/100 versus 39/100, Chained intermediates 53/120 versus 55/120, and Role-bound association 83/100 versus 80/100; every adjusted parent interval includes zero, so better faithfulness is not established. The original released Oracle Lens remains a distinct reference, not the construction or component parent. Review used exact saved text, evaluation-only contexts, original/reference outputs, retained official evidence and bounded selection traces, with no inference or judge calls and no control activations. Apparent chat verdict flips often reclassify surviving problematic quotes; the arithmetic loss keeps a visible 4 that the proposed judge omits, and one role regression preserves the direction while demanding a missing name. Higher constrained fit and recovered names/integers must not be presented as full-prose truth.
